summary: A cardholder makes a modest purchase early in the billing cycle, receives a statement, and pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario is designed to show an on-time full-payment path with the minimum-payment obligation satisfied, the account staying under the credit limit, and no late or over-limit fee being triggered.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the issuer's grace-period obligation applies to new purchases.
The credit limit is $1000.00, and the single purchase in this scenario does not cause the outstanding balance to exceed that limit.
The periodic statement closes on 2025-05-31 and sets a payment due date of 2025-06-25, providing at least 25 days after statement closing.
The cardholder pays the full statement New Balance on 2025-06-20, and the payment is credited on the date received.
No cash advances, returned payments, foreign transactions, disputed charges, or additional fees occur in this scenario.
Because the payment is made in full on or before the due date, no late fee and no over-limit fee should be assessed.
